evidence: Dorado Needle NW Ridge (MP 5.4) notes 'since the rockfall, the final block is harder': 'traverse right around it at balancy 5.7' or a 5.8ish crack; NWHikers 2019 summit-block report 'would rate this sequence 5.7'; Lemke/drdirtbag give 5.7-5.9.
note: 5.7 is the easier option around the post-2019 summit block; the direct crack is ~5.8. Pre-rockfall the step was ~5.3. Austera/Klawatti are low 5th.

evidence: MP Middle Finger Buttress - Right Side: '5.9 III (7 pitches)', FA 07/15/1973 (same date as this record's FA), 'short crux section is on the 3rd pitch' (matches the record's pitch-3 5.9).
note: No source names a 'North Buttress'; the FA date, grade, pitch count and crux pitch all match MFB Right Side.
identity: This appears to be Middle Finger Buttress - Right Side (III 5.9, 7 pitches, FA 7/15/1973), probably under an older guidebook name, not a separate line east of it.

evidence: Route listing (imported from MP) gives Gully 1 'Class 3', ~34 m; MP area: 'Descend 3rd class gully'.
Route listing (imported from MP) gives Gully 2 'Class 3', ~37 m; MP area describes the gullies as 3rd class.
Only description found: 'a prominent pinnacle called Anderson's Thumb, which involves a fun rock climb on good sandstone' (no grade). Record says Class 4 / low 5th.
note: Searched 'Anderson's Thumb'/'Andersons Thumb'/'Anderson Thumb' with Olympics, peakbagger, Climber's Guide to the Olympic Mountains (Google Sites page requires login), SummitPost lists (403). No numeric grade anywhere; 5.0 per the low-5th rule. Commitment III and AD look unsupported for a small subpeak spire, but no source corrects them.

evidence: MP: 'Easy 5th', Grade III, final 30' 'low fifth class'; SummitPost: 'the infamous chimney is 5.2'; guide listing 'II 5.2'. One party gauged the chockstone gully 5.6-5.8 and a variant face traverse 5.7.
note: Beckey's 3rd-class SW ridge now has a low-5th step at its base from glacial recession. Harder 5.6-5.8 reports are for variants/conditions around the chockstone.

evidence: Mazamas grade the route 'B' (basic glacier climb); Mountaineers run it as a Basic Glacier Climb; TR: 'dirt scramble & snow climb', 'wide-open snowslopes to the summit'; glacier is low-angle (7,000 to 6,000 ft over ~1 mi).
note: No source states a Class number; Class 2 per the non-technical-glacier rule. The approach gullies are steep loose dirt, not rock scrambling. alpine_grade 'II' is a commitment numeral that contradicts commitment III.

evidence: Both MP Mega Slab routes: thousands of feet of 4th class/low 5th slab, then '3 pitches of 5.6+' on the summit block; separate TR rates the summit-block chimney '5.6-ish'. One party soloed it, calling it 'pretty easy but exposed'.
note: The slab alone is 4th/low 5th; the grade is the summit block's.
identity: The 2005 FA matches MP's Infinite Beauty (Windham/Martin, 2005); Timeless Treasure (2004) is a parallel Mega Slab line.

evidence: Only the FA fact (Farr and Winder, 19 July 1931, via the northwest ridge) is published; a CascadeClimbers TR mentions a January 2003 solo of the 'N.W. Ridge' without a grade. No class rating found.
note: Tried 'Big Four' + northwest/NW/west ridge, Farr/Winder 1931, The Mountaineer 1931 annual (403), MP area (empty), SummitPost (403; the 'Northwest Ridge' SP hit was Mt Tyndall), CascadeClimbers (JS-gated). Class 4 is the record's value; the peak's easiest route is Class 3-4.

evidence: AAJ 1972 FA account (Guydelkon/Miller, 4000-ft north-side route): 'NCCS IV, F7'.
note: F7 mapped to 5.7. The Direct Tower Route (a different line) has 5.8 pitches. Ends with a long, steep, exposed snowfield.

evidence: AAJ FA account: '10 pitches, 4 of class four and the rest class five with occasional pins for aid. NCCS III, F7, A1'; TR cites the route as 'grade III, 5.7, 10 pitches'. MP/SummitPost: 'a difficult Pete Doorish route that has gone free at 5.10' on the east buttress.
note: No source says the Doorish 5.10 is a free ascent of the 1971 Dial-Williamson line; MP calls it 'a Pete Doorish route', so it reads as a separate line. The 1971 line's free grade is unknown (it has A1); its published grade is III 5.7 A1.
identity: The record merges the 1971 Dial-Williamson East Buttress (III 5.7 A1) with a separate Pete Doorish route on the same buttress (free at 5.10).

evidence: AAJ FA account (Davis/Holland): 'NCCS IV, F8', face 'over 3000 feet high and averaging about 70°', climbing 'mostly class 4 and 5'.
note: F8 mapped to 5.8. No repeat reports found. Also includes an exposed icefall crossing and steep snow/ice near the notch.

evidence: StephAbegg Thunder Slam: 'Booker Northwest Route' rated 3rd class, via the Booker-Buckner col; CascadeClimbers: the route from the Booker-Buckner col is class 3 with tricky route finding.
note: The col itself can be steep hard snow.

evidence: NWHikers TR (south rib from Entiat Meadows): the rib closest to camp is the least brushy, 'just a few brief class 3 steps'; another TR: 'the scramble went rather smoothly'.
note: In early season it becomes a snow climb (one party front-pointed the corniced east ridge).
